addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above 78,421.0, the high of the 14:00Z hour and the exact price that rejected this tape before the 16:00Z break. HONEST CAVEAT: that is 0.84 hourly ATRs of clean room, marginally short of the one-ATR test the desk set itself. It is accepted here because the only alternatives were gates inside the EMA wall, and because a close above 78,421.0 reclaims every hourly EMA in a single move, which is the one event that would repair today's structure.

liquidityMagnet.note: The pull is DOWN and this time the raw mass and the fresh flow agree, which was not true this morning. Over the full 23.4 hours the board is 9,181,479 USD of long liquidations against 2,772,962 USD of short, 3.31 to one. Over the last three hours it is 3,091,891 USD long against 1,219 USD short - effectively one-sided - and 94 percent of that mass landed in just two bins, 77,500 and 77,250, both of which are at or immediately around spot. Everything above 77,750 was consumed earlier and has taken nothing since. The magnet directly beneath is therefore the bin price is already standing in, and the first untouched structure below it is the 77,000.0 shelf where the new reduce gate sits. What differs from this morning is the open-interest reading. At 07:04 COT longs were dying while open interest ROSE 0.68 percent, which meant fresh shorts were replacing them. Open interest has since FALLEN 1.52 percent from 2,187,762,650.09 to 2,154,603,418.08 USD while the liquidations continued, which means positions are now LEAVING rather than flipping. Deleveraging into support is less explosive than crowded shorts into support - it removes the squeeze fuel that the 78,421.0 add gate was built to catch, and it is the main reason confidence sits at 5.50 rather than higher. The one counterweight is the 79,000 bucket, 1,583,936 USD of short-side inventory that has not been touched since the 31 August overnight.

calibration.rollingRecord: The morning reduce gate at 77,700.0 FIRED and it PAID - the first time in eleven graded sessions that acting on a fired gate has helped. The 16:00Z hour closed 77,593.0, 107.0 points under the level, and the in-flight 17:00Z hour has not reclaimed it. Spot at this stamp is 77,452.1, which is 140.9 points BELOW the trigger close, so a desk that sold at confirmation is 0.18 percent better off. acting_helped TRUE. The morning ADD gate at 78,803.3 correctly did NOT fire - the session high was 78,421.0, 382.3 points short. The one construction that came off badly was the invalidation at 77,385.5: it WAS breached, on the 16:00Z wick to 77,320.0, 65.5 points through, and then price closed back above it and sits 66.6 points above it now. So two of three constructions worked cleanly and the third failed by a wick of 65 points.
calibration.note: The finding validates the rule change morning made, and it is worth being precise about why. Morning stopped widening gates and started PLACING them - it moved the reduce level below the last live liquidation bucket (77,750) and onto a floor that had been defended twice, rather than pushing it further away in ATR terms. That gate fired and paid. The ten previous failures were all gates sitting inside live liquidation flow, where the level gets run by the flow itself and then un-run. This session keeps the placement rule and applies it identically: the new 77,000.0 reduce gate sits below the 77,250 bucket that is taking fills right now and below the 77,500 bucket that was consumed on the break, on the 30 August daily low, with the 28 August low at 76,888.0 as the second line. One caveat against reading too much into a single win: the gate paid by 0.18 percent, which is small enough to be noise, and the sample is one. The rule needs two or three more confirmations before it is more than a hypothesis. The separate lesson from the invalidation wick is that a level 632.5 points under spot was still reachable inside one hour on an oil-shock tape - on days like this, intraday distance in ATRs understates the real risk.
